fullPassage: We cannot make sense of the facts of the past unless they are embedded in stories of agents negotiating the world. These stories must connect actors' goals, desires, and intentions to their experiences, and ultimately to their actions and interactions with others. When historical records can be fit neatly into one story, they seem to make sense. But problems arise when the same records could fit equally well into two or more different narratives. When this happens, what used to seem like a clear explanation becomes _______________. In other words, the very same records that looked like solid evidence for one story can just as easily be used to support a completely different one. This doesn't mean historical records are useless — it means their meaning depends on the narrative framework within which they are placed.

questions.passage: These stories must connect actors' goals, desires, and intentions to their experiences, and ultimately to their actions and __________ with others. (interact)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: interact(동사: 상호작용하다) → interactions(명사: 상호작용)
det.analysis: actions and __________(interact) with others — and로 actions과 병렬 연결되므로 명사형 interactions가 필요.
det.tip: actions and interactions에서 and가 두 명사를 병렬 연결한다. interact(동사)를 명사형 interactions로 변환해야 한다.

questions.passage: When this happens, what used to seem like a clear __________ becomes questionable. (explain)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: explain(동사: 설명하다) → explanation(명사: 설명)
det.analysis: a clear __________(explain) — 관사 a와 형용사 clear 뒤에 명사가 필요. explain(동사)를 명사형 explanation으로 변환.
det.tip: a clear explanation에서 관사(a) + 형용사(clear) 뒤에는 명사가 와야 한다. explain → explanation은 동사 → 명사 변환.

questions.passage: We cannot make sense of the facts of the past unless they are embedded in stories of agents negotiating the world. These stories must connect actors' goals, desires, and intentions to their experiences, and ultimately to their actions and interactions with others. When historical records can be fit neatly into one story, they seem to make sense. But problems arise when the same records could fit equally well into two or more different narratives. When this happens, what used to seem like a clear explanation becomes _______________. In other words, the very same records that looked like solid evidence for one story can just as easily be used to support a completely different one. This doesn't mean historical records are useless — it means their meaning depends on the __________ within which they are placed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기록의 의미는 그것이 놓이는 ___에 달려 있다.
det.analysis:
① narrative framework: 서사적 틀 — 원문의 핵심 결론 표현, 기록의 의미가 달라지는 맥락의 틀 ←정답
② solid evidence: 확실한 증거 — 기록이 증거처럼 보인다는 표현이지 의미가 달려 있는 대상이 아님
③ historical records: 역사적 기록 — 기록이 기록에 달려 있다는 동어반복
④ different narratives: 다른 서사들 — 복수 표현이고 within which 구문과 맞지 않음
det.tip: the narrative framework within which they are placed — 기록이 놓이는 서사적 틀이 글의 최종 결론.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 과거의 사실들은 ___의 이야기 속에 내장되어야만 이해할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
① agents negotiating the world: 세상을 헤쳐나가는 행위자들 — 원문의 핵심 표현 ←정답
② stories of the past: 과거의 이야기 — stories of agents이지 stories of the past가 아님
③ actions and interactions: 행동과 상호작용 — 이야기의 연결 대상이지 이야기의 주체가 아님
④ goals and desires: 목표와 욕구 — 행위자의 속성이지 이야기의 주인공이 아님
det.tip: stories of agents negotiating the world — 세상을 헤쳐나가는 행위자들의 이야기. 글의 첫 문장 핵심 구절.
